boundaries.note: The 81 il as OpenStreetMap draws them; shapeISO is TR-01..TR-81, the plaka codes.

admin1.note: Read for the name_tr/name_en pair only; the boundaries come from geoBoundaries.

countries.note: Neighbouring countries, drawn as context and never as data.

lakes.note: Van, Tuz and the rest, painted over the province fill so they are not land.

roads.note: The reference road network. Not a highway map: 1 304 segments cover Türkiye, and KGM's own network cannot be reproduced here (CLAUDE.md §3).

names.command: -i {admin1} -filter "iso_a2 === 'TR'" -each "code = +iso_3166_2.slice(3), name_tr = name_tr || name, name_en = name_en || name" -filter-fields code,name_tr,name_en -o {raw}/province-names.csv format=csv

provinces.command: -i {boundaries} -each "code = +shapeISO.slice(3)" -filter-fields code -join {raw}/province-names.csv keys=code,code field-types=code:number -simplify 2% keep-shapes -clean -o {out}/provinces.json format=geojson precision=0.0001 id-field=code

provinces-detail.command: -i {boundaries} -each "code = +shapeISO.slice(3)" -filter-fields code -join {raw}/province-names.csv keys=code,code field-types=code:number -simplify 15% keep-shapes -clean -o {out}/provinces-detail.json format=geojson precision=0.00001 id-field=code

roads.command: -i {roads} -clip bbox=25,35,45.5,42.5 -filter "type !== 'Ferry Route' && type !== 'Ferry, seasonal' && type !== 'Track'" -each "kind = type || '', label = label || ''" -filter-fields kind,label -simplify 15% keep-shapes -o {out}/roads.json format=geojson precision=0.001

notes: Natural Earth is pinned at tag v5.1.2 and geoBoundaries at commit 9469f09; a moving source would change coastlines with no commit.
The province shapes are geoBoundaries' (OpenStreetMap-derived); the name_tr/name_en pair is joined on from Natural Earth.
shapeISO TR-01..TR-81 are the plaka codes, which YSK's il_ID and TÜİK's province tables also use.
Each outline is dissolved from the already-simplified provinces of its own tier, so the outline sits exactly on the fills.
The DETAIL tier is what coordinates are placed against and what the declared geometry checks use; the overview tier is only drawn.
Türkiye's own TUCBS geodata forbids redistribution, which is why the boundaries here are not the government's.
